source.text: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Σάρδεσιν ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἔχων τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀστέρας· Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα, ὅτι ὄνομα ἔχεις ὅτι ζῇς, καὶ νεκρὸς εἶ.

records.literal_gloss: And to the angel of the in Sardis church write: These things says the [one] having the seven spirits of the God and the seven stars: I know of you the works, that a name you have that you live, and dead you are.

en.L: And to the angel of the church in Sardis write: "These things says the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, and you are dead.
en.B: To the angel of the church in Sardis, write: "This is the message of the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works. People speak of you as alive, but you are dead.
en.R: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Sardis: "This message is from the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. I know everything you do. People think you are alive, but you are really dead.

fr.L: Et à l’ange de l’église de Sardes, écris : « Voici ce que dit celui qui a les sept esprits de Dieu et les sept étoiles : je connais tes œuvres ; tu as un nom de vivant, et tu es mort.
fr.B: À l’ange de l’église de Sardes, écris : « Voici le message de celui qui a les sept esprits de Dieu et les sept étoiles : je connais tes œuvres. On dit que tu es vivant, mais tu es mort.
fr.R: Écris cette lettre à l’ange de l’église de Sardes : « Ce message vient de celui qui a les sept esprits de Dieu et les sept étoiles. Je sais tout ce que tu fais. Les gens pensent que tu es vivant, mais en réalité tu es mort.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the seven spirits of God
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:4. Here the seven spirits belong to God and are held by Christ, together with the seven stars, the angels of the churches (1:20). A church that is dead is addressed by the one who has the Spirit who gives life.

decisions.choice: a name for being alive: a reputation that does not match the truth
decisions.reason: ὄνομα, "name", here means what people say of the church, its reputation. Others see a living church; Christ sees a dead one. The contrast matches the one in 2:9, where a poor church is rich.

decisions.choice: Sardis: an old royal city, famous for a citadel that was taken by surprise
decisions.reason: Sardis had been the capital of the kingdom of Lydia and was proud of its past. Its citadel on a steep hill was thought impossible to take, yet it fell to Cyrus of Persia in 547 BC and to Antiochus III in about 214 BC when the defenders did not keep watch. The call to wake up and the warning about a thief (3:2-3) would have meant something to its people. The city was badly damaged by an earthquake in AD 17 and rebuilt.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

source.text: γίνου γρηγορῶν, καὶ στήρισον τὰ λοιπὰ ἃ ἔμελλον ἀποθανεῖν, οὐ γὰρ εὕρηκά σου τὰ ἔργα πεπληρωμένα ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ μου·

records.literal_gloss: Become watching, and strengthen the remaining things which were about to die, for not I have found of you the works fulfilled before the God of me.

en.L: Be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die, for I have not found your works complete before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God.
en.B: Become watchful, and put strength into what remains and was on the point of dying, for I have found that your works are not complete before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God.
en.R: Wake up! Make strong what little is still alive in you before it dies too. I have seen what you do, and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God's eyes it is not finished.

fr.L: Sois vigilant, et affermis ce qui reste, qui allait mourir, car je n’ai pas trouvé tes œuvres accomplies devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu.
fr.B: Deviens vigilant, et fortifie ce qui reste et qui était sur le point de mourir, car j’ai constaté que tes œuvres ne sont pas achevées devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu.
fr.R: Réveille-toi ! Rends fort le peu de vie qui te reste, avant qu’il meure lui aussi. J’ai vu ce que tu fais, et aux yeux de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, ce n’est pas terminé.

decisions.choice: become watchful: wake up and stay awake
decisions.reason: γίνου γρηγορῶν means more than "watch": the church is asleep and must become watchful and remain so. The same verb comes back in 3:3 and 16:15.

decisions.choice: what remains: whatever life is left in the church
decisions.reason: λοιπὰ is neuter, "the things that remain", so it most likely means what is left of the church's life and works, though the faithful few of 3:4 belong to it. "Were about to die" is said from the readers' point of view: when they hear the letter, those things are close to death.

decisions.choice: complete: carried through to the end
decisions.reason: πεπληρωμένα means filled or completed. The works were begun but not finished, and before God they fall short.

decisions.choice: my God: Jesus speaks of God as his God
decisions.reason: The risen Jesus calls God "my God" (3:12, four times; compare John 20:17), as he calls him "my Father" (2:28; 3:5, 21).

decisions.choice: Wake up (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain command a young reader would use; Literal and Balanced keep the sense of becoming watchful.

source.text: μνημόνευε οὖν πῶς εἴληφας καὶ ἤκουσας καὶ τήρει, καὶ μετανόησον· ἐὰν οὖν μὴ γρηγορήσῃς, ἥξω ὡς κλέπτης, καὶ οὐ μὴ γνῷς ποίαν ὥραν ἥξω ἐπὶ σέ·

records.literal_gloss: Remember therefore how you have received and heard, and keep [it], and repent. If therefore not you watch, I will come like a thief, and not not you know what hour I will come upon you.

en.L: Remember, then, how you have received and heard, and keep [it], and repent. So if you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will certainly not know at what hour I will come upon you.
en.B: Think back, then, to the way you received the message and heard it. Keep it, and repent. If you stay asleep, I will come like a thief, and you will never know the hour when I come against you.
en.R: So remember the message you were given and heard. Obey it, and turn away from your sins. If you do not wake up, I will come when you do not expect me, as a thief does. You will not know what time I will come to judge you.

fr.L: Souviens-toi donc de la manière dont tu as reçu et entendu, et garde-[le], et repens-toi. Si donc tu ne veilles pas, je viendrai comme un voleur, et tu ne sauras certainement pas à quelle heure je viendrai sur toi.
fr.B: Rappelle-toi donc comment tu as reçu le message et comment tu l’as entendu. Garde-le, et repens-toi. Si tu restes endormi, je viendrai comme un voleur, et tu ne sauras jamais à quelle heure je viendrai contre toi.
fr.R: Alors souviens-toi du message qu’on t’a donné et que tu as entendu. Obéis-lui, et détourne-toi de tes péchés. Si tu ne te réveilles pas, je viendrai quand tu ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}attendras pas, comme un voleur. Tu ne sauras pas à quel moment je viendrai pour te juger.

decisions.choice: how you received and heard: the gospel message, and the way they first welcomed it
decisions.reason: πῶς means "how". It points both to the message they were given and to the eager way they once took it in. The object of "keep" is the message itself.

decisions.choice: like a thief: Jesus's own picture of a coming no one expects
decisions.reason: Jesus said that the Son of Man would come like a thief in the night (Matthew 24:43-44; Luke 12:39-40), and Paul and Peter repeat it (1 Thessalonians 5:2; 2 Peter 3:10). Revelation uses it again in 16:15.

decisions.choice: I will come upon you: a coming in judgment on this church
decisions.reason: As in 2:5, the coming depends on whether the church wakes up and is aimed at this church: ἐπὶ σέ, "upon you", has the sense of "against you". It is most likely a visit of judgment, though Jesus's words about the thief speak of his final coming.

decisions.choice: the message (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no object for "received" and "heard". Balanced and Readable supply "the message" (m1).

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἔχεις ὀλίγα ὀνόματα ἐν Σάρδεσιν ἃ οὐκ ἐμόλυναν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτῶν, καὶ περιπατήσουσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν λευκοῖς, ὅτι ἄξιοί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: But you have a few names in Sardis which not soiled the garments of them, and they will walk with me in white, because worthy they are.

en.L: But you have a few names in Sardis that have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in white, because they are worthy.
en.B: Still, you have a few people in Sardis who have not stained their clothes. They will walk with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dressed in white, for they deserve it.
en.R: But a few people in Sardis have kept their clothes clean. They have not let sin make them dirty. They will walk with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, wearing white clothes, because they are worthy.

fr.L: Mais tu as quelques noms à Sardes qui n’ont pas souillé leurs vêtements, et ils marcheront avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} en blanc, parce qu’ils sont dignes.
fr.B: Pourtant, tu as à Sardes quelques personnes qui n’ont pas taché leurs vêtements. Elles marcheront avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, vêtues de blanc, car elles en sont dignes.
fr.R: Mais quelques personnes à Sardes ont gardé leurs vêtements propres. Elles n’ont pas laissé le péché les salir. Elles marcheront avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, habillées de blanc, parce qu’elles en sont dignes.

decisions.choice: a few names: a few people
decisions.reason: "Names" stands for persons, as in Acts 1:15 ("a crowd of names"). After the "name" of 3:1, the word may also suggest people whose names are known to Christ.

decisions.choice: garments not soiled: lives not stained by sin and compromise
decisions.reason: Clothing stands for a person's life and conduct, as in Zechariah 3:3-5 and Revelation 7:14. Soiled clothes are a life stained by sin; the few in Sardis have kept themselves clean.

decisions.choice: in white: the clothing of purity, victory and celebration
decisions.reason: White clothes were worn at festivals and stood for purity and joy. In Revelation the faithful and the angels are dressed in white (3:5, 18; 4:4; 6:11; 7:9, 13-14; 19:14).

decisions.choice: They have not let sin make them dirty (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of soiled clothes (m2).

source.text: ὁ νικῶν οὕτως περιβαλεῖται ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ οὐ μὴ ἐξαλείψω τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῆς βίβλου τῆς ζωῆς, καὶ ὁμολογήσω τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐνώπιον τοῦ πατρός μου καὶ ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] overcoming thus will be clothed in garments white, and not not I will blot out the name of him from the book of the life, and I will confess the name of him before the Father of me and before the angels of him.

en.L: The one who overcomes will in this way be clothed in white garments, and I will certainly not erase {{gender:that person's|his}} name from the book of life, and I will acknowledge {{gender:that person's|his}} name before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels.
en.B: Everyone who overcomes will be clothed in this way, in white. I will never erase {{gender:their|his}} name from the book of life. Before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels I will openly own {{gender:their|his}} name.
en.R: Everyone who wins the victory will wear white clothes like these. I will never remove {{gender:their|his}} name from the book of life. I will tell {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels that {{gender:they belong|he belongs}} to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Celui qui est vainqueur sera ainsi revêtu de vêtements blancs, et je n’effacerai certainement pas son nom du livre de la vie, et je reconnaîtrai son nom devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et devant {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges.
fr.B: Tout vainqueur sera ainsi vêtu de blanc. Je n’effacerai jamais son nom du livre de vie. Devant {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et devant {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges, je reconnaîtrai ouvertement son nom.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui remportent la victoire porteront des vêtements blancs comme ceux-là. Je n’enlèverai jamais leur nom du livre de vie. Je dirai à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père et à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} anges qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiennent.

decisions.choice: in this way: like the faithful few of 3:4
decisions.reason: οὕτως links the promise to 3:4: the one who overcomes will be dressed in white as they will be.

decisions.choice: the book of life: God's list of those who belong to him
decisions.reason: Cities kept lists of their citizens, and a name could be struck off. The Old Testament speaks of God's book in the same way (Exodus 32:32-33; Psalm 69:29; Daniel 12:1). In Revelation, the names in the book of life are those who belong to the Lamb (13:8; 20:12, 15; 21:27). The promise is put negatively and strongly: "I will certainly not erase".

decisions.choice: acknowledging the name: an echo of Jesus's saying in the Gospels
decisions.reason: Jesus said, "Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I will acknowledge before my Father in heaven" (Matthew 10:32; Luke 12:8, "before the angels of God"). ὁμολογήσω means to declare openly that someone is one's own.

decisions.choice: erase (L, B); remove (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means to wipe out writing. "Blot out" is older English; "erase" says the same in modern English.

decisions.choice: "son nom" (L, B), "leur nom" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English needs {{gender:their|his}}, French "son" refers back to "celui qui est vainqueur" or "tout vainqueur", which already means anyone, and "son" does not show the owner's sex. As the style guide says (section 7), no setting is needed; the same holds for "quelqu'un ... lui" in 3:20.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

en.L: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
en.B: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."
en.R: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."

fr.L: Que celui qui a une oreille entende ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.B: Que celui qui a des oreilles écoute ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.R: Que tous ceux qui peuvent entendre écoutent bien ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.

source.text: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Φιλαδελφείᾳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ ἅγιος, ὁ ἀληθινός, ὁ ἔχων τὴν κλεῖν Δαυίδ, ὁ ἀνοίγων καὶ οὐδεὶς κλείσει, καὶ κλείων καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀνοίγει·

records.literal_gloss: And to the angel of the in Philadelphia church write: These things says the holy [one], the true [one], the [one] having the key of David, the [one] opening and no one will shut, and shutting and no one opens:

en.L: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write: "These things says the holy one, the true one, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut, and shuts and no one opens:
en.B: To the angel of the church in Philadelphia, write: "This is the message of the holy and true one, the one with the key of David: when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opens, no one will shut, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shuts, no one opens:
en.R: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Philadelphia: "This message is from the one who is holy and true. He holds the key of David the king. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opens a door, no one can shut it. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shuts a door, no one can open it.

fr.L: Et à l’ange de l’église de Philadelphie, écris : « Voici ce que dit le saint, le véritable, celui qui a la clé de David, celui qui ouvre et personne ne fermera, et qui ferme et personne n’ouvre :
fr.B: À l’ange de l’église de Philadelphie, écris : « Voici le message de celui qui est saint et vrai, de celui qui a la clé de David : quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ouvre, personne ne fermera, et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferme, personne n’ouvre :
fr.R: Écris cette lettre à l’ange de l’église de Philadelphie : « Ce message vient de celui qui est saint et vrai. Il tient la clé du roi David. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ouvre une porte, personne ne peut la fermer. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ferme une porte, personne ne peut l’ouvrir.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: holy and true: titles of God
decisions.reason: "The Holy One" is a name of God in the Old Testament (Isaiah 40:25), and in Revelation 6:10 the martyrs call God "holy and true". ἀληθινός means true in the sense of genuine and faithful to his word. Christ bears God's titles, as in 1:17.

decisions.choice: the key of David: Isaiah 22:22
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 22:22 God gives Eliakim, steward of the king's palace, "the key of the house of David": what he opens no one shuts, and what he shuts no one opens. Christ holds that authority over the kingdom of David, deciding who may enter. Compare the keys of death and Hades in 1:18.

decisions.choice: Philadelphia: the youngest of the seven cities
decisions.reason: Philadelphia was founded in the second century BC and named after a king of Pergamum who was known for his love for his brother (the name means "brotherly love"). It lay on a main road to the east and suffered often from earthquakes, including the great one of AD 17.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

source.text: Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ἐνώπιόν σου θύραν ἠνεῳγμένην, ἣν οὐδεὶς δύναται κλεῖσαι αὐτήν ὅτι μικρὰν ἔχεις δύναμιν, καὶ ἐτήρησάς μου τὸν λόγον, καὶ οὐκ ἠρνήσω τὸ ὄνομά μου.

records.literal_gloss: I know of you the works—behold I have given before you a door having been opened, which no one is able to shut it—that little you have power, and you kept of me the word and not denied the name of me.

en.L: I know your works—look, I have set before you an opened door, which no one can shut—that you have little power, and you kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word and did not deny {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.B: I know your works. Look: I have opened a door for you, and no one can shut it. Your strength is small, yet you have kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, and you have not disowned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.R: I know everything you do. Look! I have opened a door for you, and no one can shut it. I know you are not very strong. But you have obeyed what I said, and you have not denied that you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

fr.L: Je connais tes œuvres — voici, j’ai placé devant toi une porte ouverte, que personne ne peut fermer — [je sais] que tu as peu de puissance, et tu as gardé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole et tu n’as pas renié {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.
fr.B: Je connais tes œuvres. Voici : j’ai ouvert une porte devant toi, et personne ne peut la fermer. Tu n’as que peu de force, et pourtant tu as gardé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} parole et tu n’as pas renié {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.
fr.R: Je sais tout ce que tu fais. Regarde ! J’ai ouvert une porte pour toi, et personne ne peut la fermer. Je sais que tu n’es pas très fort. Mais tu as obéi à ce que j’ai dit, et tu n’as pas nié que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiens.

decisions.choice: an open door: entry into the kingdom, and perhaps an opportunity to spread the gospel
decisions.reason: After the key of David in 3:7, the open door most likely means that Christ has opened the way into his kingdom for this church, whatever others say (3:9). Paul uses an open door for a chance to preach (1 Corinthians 16:9; 2 Corinthians 2:12; Colossians 4:3), and that sense may be present as well.

decisions.choice: the open door is set in the middle; "that" goes back to "I know"
alternatives: "because": the door is opened because they have kept his word
decisions.reason: "Look, I have set before you an open door" breaks into the sentence, and ὅτι most likely continues "I know your works": I know that you have little power. It could also give the reason for the open door.

decisions.choice: little power: a small and weak church
decisions.reason: The church had little strength, in numbers or standing, yet it kept Christ's word under pressure and did not deny him.

decisions.choice: the open door as its own sentence (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the break in the sentence with dashes. Balanced and Readable give the open door a sentence of its own and read "that" as continuing "I know" (m2).

source.text: ἰδοὺ διδῶ ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τοῦ Σατανᾶ, τῶν λεγόντων ἑαυτοὺς Ἰουδαίους εἶναι, καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν ἀλλὰ ψεύδονται ἰδοὺ ποιήσω αὐτοὺς ἵνα ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιον τῶν ποδῶν σου, καὶ γνῶσιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἠγάπησά σε.

records.literal_gloss: Behold I give from the synagogue of the Satan, of those saying themselves Jews to be, and not they are but they lie—behold I will make them so that they will come and will bow down before the feet of you, and they will know that I loved you.

en.L: Look, I am giving [some] from the synagogue of Satan, of those who say they are Jews, and are not, but lie—look, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and know that I have loved you.
en.B: Look at what I will do with those from Satan's synagogue, who claim to be Jews and are not, but lie: I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will learn that I have loved you.
en.R: Some people say they are Jews, but they are lying. They belong to Satan's synagogue. Listen! I will make them come and bow down at your feet. They will know that I love you.

fr.L: Voici, je [te] donne [des gens] de la synagogue de Satan, de ceux qui se disent juifs et ne le sont pas, mais mentent — voici, je les ferai venir se prosterner devant tes pieds, et ils sauront que je t’ai aimé.
fr.B: Voici ce que je ferai de ceux de la synagogue de Satan, qui prétendent être juifs et ne le sont pas, mais qui mentent : je les ferai venir se prosterner à tes pieds, et ils sauront que je t’ai aimé.
fr.R: Certains disent qu’ils sont juifs, mais ils mentent. Ils appartiennent à la synagogue de Satan. Écoute ! Je les ferai venir se mettre à genoux devant toi. Ils sauront que je t’aime.

decisions.choice: a local group who opposed the church, as in Smyrna
decisions.reason: See the note on 2:9. The words are about a group in Philadelphia who denied that the believers belonged to God. They are not a statement about the Jewish people and give no ground for hostility toward them.

decisions.choice: Isaiah's promise turned around
decisions.reason: Isaiah promised that the nations who oppressed Israel would come and bow down at Israel's feet and know that God had loved his people (Isaiah 60:14; 49:23; 43:4). Here those who claim to be the people of God will come and bow before a church of Jews and Gentiles who follow Jesus, and will learn that Christ has loved them.

decisions.choice: bow down: an act of homage, not worship of the believers
decisions.reason: προσκυνήσουσιν means to bow low, and is often used of worship. Revelation forbids worship of anyone but God (19:10; 22:8-9), so here it means the homage of those who acknowledge they were wrong, as in Isaiah. The bowing is "before your feet"; the honor goes to the one who loved them.

decisions.choice: a sentence that starts twice
decisions.reason: The Greek begins "Look, I am giving some from the synagogue of Satan", breaks off, and starts again: "look, I will make them come". The second "look" takes up the first.

decisions.choice: one smooth sentence (B); short sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the broken sentence (m4) with a dash; Balanced and Readable make it read as one statement.

source.text: ὅτι ἐτήρησας τὸν λόγον τῆς ὑπομονῆς μου, κἀγώ σε τηρήσω ἐκ τῆς ὥρας τοῦ πειρασμοῦ τῆς μελλούσης ἔρχεσθαι ἐπὶ τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, πειράσαι τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Because you kept the word of the endurance of me, I also you will keep from the hour of the testing the being about to come upon the world whole to test those dwelling on the earth.

en.L: Because you kept the word of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who live on the earth.
en.B: You have kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} call to endure, and so I in turn will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come over the whole world, to put the people of the earth to the test.
en.R: You obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when I told you to keep going. So I will keep you safe from the time of testing that is coming. It will come on the whole world to test everyone who lives on the earth.

fr.L: Parce que tu as gardé la parole de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} persévérance, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi je te garderai de l’heure de l’épreuve qui va venir sur le monde entier, pour éprouver ceux qui habitent sur la terre.
fr.B: Tu as gardé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} appel à la persévérance ; c’est pourquoi, {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je te garderai de l’heure de l’épreuve qui va venir sur le monde entier pour mettre à l’épreuve les habitants de la terre.
fr.R: Tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as obéi quand je t’ai dit de tenir bon. Alors je te mettrai à l’abri du temps de l’épreuve qui arrive. Elle viendra sur le monde entier pour éprouver tous ceux qui habitent sur la terre.

decisions.choice: the word of my endurance: my command to endure, or the message of the endurance I showed
decisions.reason: "My endurance" can mean the endurance Christ calls for or the endurance he showed in his own suffering, which believers share (1:9). Either way, they have held to his word and kept going.

decisions.choice: keep from the hour of testing: protect them from it, whether by sparing them from it or keeping them safe through it
alternatives: keep them out of that time altogether
keep them faithful while it lasts
decisions.reason: τηρήσω ἐκ can mean to keep someone away from a thing or to guard them from its harm. The same phrase in John 17:15 means kept from the evil one while still in the world. The sentence promises protection; it does not say whether the church will be taken out of the time of testing or kept safe within it. The wordplay is clear: because you kept my word, I will keep you.

decisions.choice: those who live on the earth: the people of the world who oppose God
decisions.reason: In Revelation this phrase usually means the world's people in their opposition to God, those who persecute the faithful and worship the beast (6:10; 8:13; 11:10; 13:8, 12, 14; 17:8). The testing comes on them; the church is kept.

decisions.choice: keep you from (L, B); keep you safe from (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the open phrase "keep from" (m2). Readable adds "safe" to say that the promise is protection, without deciding how it is given.

decisions.choice: "je te mettrai à l'abri du temps de l'épreuve" (R)
decisions.reason: Like the English "keep you safe from", "mettre à l'abri de" says that the promise is protection without deciding whether it is given by sparing them the testing or by keeping them through it (m2). The other wordings would each decide it.

source.text: ἔρχομαι ταχύ· κράτει ὃ ἔχεις, ἵνα μηδεὶς λάβῃ τὸν στέφανόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: I am coming quickly; hold fast what you have, so that no one takes the crown of you.

en.L: I am coming soon. Hold fast what you have, so that no one takes your crown.
en.B: I am coming soon. Keep a firm grip on what you have, so that no one takes your crown.
en.R: I am coming soon. Hold on tightly to what you have. Then no one will take away your prize, the winner's crown.

fr.L: Je viens bientôt. Tiens ferme ce que tu as, afin que personne ne prenne ta couronne.
fr.B: Je viens bientôt. Garde fermement ce que tu as, pour que personne ne te prenne ta couronne.
fr.R: Je viens bientôt. Tiens bon et garde bien ce que tu as. Alors personne ne t’enlèvera ton prix, la couronne du vainqueur.

decisions.choice: I am coming soon: the final coming, as a comfort
decisions.reason: Unlike the warnings in 2:5, 16 and 3:3, here the coming has no condition and is good news to a faithful church.

decisions.choice: your crown: the winner's wreath
decisions.reason: See the note on 2:10. The crown is already theirs, if they hold on; no one can take it unless they let go.

source.text: ὁ νικῶν ποιήσω αὐτὸν στῦλον ἐν τῷ ναῷ τοῦ θεοῦ μου, καὶ ἔξω οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃ ἔτι, καὶ γράψω ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ μου καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς πόλεως τοῦ θεοῦ μου, τῆς καινῆς Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ καταβαίνουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ μου, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου τὸ καινόν.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] overcoming, I will make him a pillar in the temple of the God of me, and outside not not he will go out anymore, and I will write on him the name of the God of me and the name of the city of the God of me, the new Jerusalem, the [one] coming down out of the heaven from the God of me, and the name of me the new.

en.L: The one who overcomes, I will make {{gender:that person|him}} a pillar in the temple of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, and {{gender:that person|he}} will certainly not go out of it again, and I will write on {{gender:that person|him}} the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God and the name of the city of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} new name.
en.B: I will make everyone who overcomes a pillar in the temple of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, never again to go out of it. On {{gender:them|him}} I will write the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, and the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God's city, the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own new name.
en.R: I will make everyone who wins the victory like a pillar in the temple of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God. They will never have to leave it. I will write on them the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God. I will write the name of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God's city, the new Jerusalem, which comes down from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God out of heaven. And I will write on them {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} new name.

fr.L: Celui qui est vainqueur, je ferai de lui une colonne dans le temple de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, et il n’en sortira certainement plus jamais ; et j’écrirai sur lui le nom de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu et le nom de la cité de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, la nouvelle Jérusalem, qui descend du ciel d’auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom nouveau.
fr.B: Je ferai de tout vainqueur une colonne dans le temple de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, et il n’en sortira plus jamais. J’écrirai sur lui le nom de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, le nom de la ville de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, la nouvelle Jérusalem qui descend du ciel d’auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} propre nom nouveau.
fr.R: Tous ceux qui remportent la victoire, je ferai d’eux comme une colonne dans le temple de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu. Ils n’auront plus jamais à en sortir. J’écrirai sur eux le nom de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu. J’écrirai le nom de la ville de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, la nouvelle Jérusalem, qui descend du ciel, d’auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu. Et j’écrirai sur eux {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom nouveau.

decisions.choice: a pillar in the temple: a lasting place in God's presence
decisions.reason: A pillar stands firm and stays where it is set. Leaders could be called pillars (Galatians 2:9). The one who overcomes will have a permanent place with God and will never have to leave. In the new Jerusalem there is no temple building, for God and the Lamb are its temple (21:22): the picture is of belonging to God's presence.

decisions.choice: never again going out: a promise to a city that often had to flee
decisions.reason: Philadelphia was shaken by frequent earthquakes, and the geographer Strabo, writing in the early first century, says that many of its people lived outside the city for fear of them. A promise of a place they would never have to leave would have spoken to them, though the text does not refer to this directly.

decisions.choice: names written on them: they belong to God, to his city, and to Christ
decisions.reason: A name written on someone marks them as belonging to its owner (compare 7:3; 14:1; 22:4). The one who overcomes is marked as God's own, a citizen of the new Jerusalem (21:2, 10), and Christ's, who has a new name (2:17; 19:12).

decisions.choice: like a pillar (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison so that a young reader does not take it literally.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

en.L: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
en.B: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."
en.R: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."

fr.L: Que celui qui a une oreille entende ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.B: Que celui qui a des oreilles écoute ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.R: Que tous ceux qui peuvent entendre écoutent bien ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.

source.text: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ Ἀμήν, ὁ μάρτυς ὁ πιστὸς καὶ ἀληθινός, ἡ ἀρχὴ τῆς κτίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And to the angel of the in Laodicea church write: These things says the Amen, the witness the faithful and true, the beginning of the creation of the God:

en.L: And to the angel of the church in Laodicea write: "These things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God's creation:
en.B: To the angel of the church in Laodicea, write: "This is the message of the Amen, the witness who is faithful and true, the origin of God's creation:
en.R: Write this letter to the angel of the church in Laodicea: "This message is from the one who is called the Amen. He is the witness who is faithful and always tells the truth. Everything God made had its beginning in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Et à l’ange de l’église de Laodicée, écris : « Voici ce que dit l’Amen, le témoin fidèle et véritable, le commencement de la création de Dieu :
fr.B: À l’ange de l’église de Laodicée, écris : « Voici le message de l’Amen, du témoin fidèle et véritable, de l’origine de la création de Dieu :
fr.R: Écris cette lettre à l’ange de l’église de Laodicée : « Ce message vient de celui qu’on appelle l’Amen. Il est le témoin fidèle, qui dit toujours la vérité. Tout ce que Dieu a créé a eu son commencement en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the Amen: the one in whom God's word is true and sure
decisions.reason: "Amen" means "it is so, it is sure". Isaiah 65:16 speaks of "the God of amen", the God of truth. Christ is God's "Amen", the one through whom all God's promises are "yes" (2 Corinthians 1:20). The title fits a letter to a church that is neither one thing nor the other.

decisions.choice: the beginning of God's creation: its source and origin, the one through whom it came to be
decisions.reason: ἀρχὴ can mean beginning, first cause, or ruler. Revelation gives Christ the titles of God, "the first and the last" and "the beginning and the end" (1:17; 22:13), so he is not here counted among the things God made. The sense is that creation has its origin in him, as John 1:3 and Colossians 1:15-18 say, and that he rules over it.

decisions.choice: Laodicea: a wealthy city of banking, cloth and medicine
decisions.reason: Laodicea lay in the Lycus valley near Colossae and Hierapolis (Colossians 4:13-16). It was rich from banking and trade, known for cloth woven from glossy black wool, and had a school of medicine. After the earthquake of AD 60 it rebuilt itself without help from Rome, according to Tacitus. The letter's gold, white clothes and eye salve (3:18) answer these sources of the city's pride.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

decisions.choice: beginning (L); origin (B); had its beginning in him (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open word "beginning". Balanced and Readable say "origin" and "had its beginning in him" to avoid the reading that Christ was the first thing created (m3).

source.text: Οἶδά σου τὰ ἔργα, ὅτι οὔτε ψυχρὸς εἶ οὔτε ζεστός.

records.literal_gloss: I know of you the works, that neither cold you are nor hot.

en.L: I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot.
en.B: I know your works: you are not cold, and you are not hot.
en.R: I know everything you do. You are not cold, and you are not hot.

fr.L: Je connais tes œuvres : tu n’es ni froid ni chaud.
fr.B: Je connais tes œuvres : tu n’es pas froid, et tu n’es pas chaud.
fr.R: Je sais tout ce que tu fais. Tu n’es pas froid, et tu n’es pas chaud.

decisions.choice: neither cold nor hot: of no use, like tepid water
alternatives: neither against Christ nor fervent for him
decisions.reason: The picture is usually taken to mean spiritual temperature: cold is hostile, hot is eager. But Christ wishes they were either (3:15), and he would hardly wish them hostile. More likely cold and hot are both good: cold water refreshes, hot water heals, and lukewarm water does neither. The neighboring city of Hierapolis had hot springs, and Colossae had cold water, while Laodicea's water came by aqueduct. Whether the picture draws on that is not certain.

source.text: ὄφελον ψυχρὸς ἦς ἢ ζεστός.

records.literal_gloss: Would that cold you were or hot.

en.L: I wish you were cold or hot.
en.B: If only you were one or the other, cold or hot!
en.R: I wish you were either cold or hot!

fr.L: Je voudrais que tu sois froid ou chaud.
fr.B: Si seulement tu étais l’un ou l’autre, froid ou chaud !
fr.R: J’aimerais tellement que tu sois froid ou chaud !

decisions.choice: a wish that cannot now be fulfilled
decisions.reason: ὄφελον with a past tense expresses a wish about the present that is not so: "if only you were". See the note on 3:15a on what cold and hot mean.

source.text: οὕτως, ὅτι χλιαρὸς εἶ καὶ οὔτε ζεστὸς οὔτε ψυχρός, μέλλω σε ἐμέσαι ἐκ τοῦ στόματός μου.

records.literal_gloss: So because lukewarm you are, and neither hot nor cold, I am about you to vomit out of the mouth of me.

en.L: So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth.
en.B: As it is, you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, and so I am about to spew you out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth.
en.R: But you are only lukewarm, neither hot nor cold. So I am going to spit you out of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth, like water that tastes bad.

fr.L: Ainsi, parce que tu es tiède, et ni chaud ni froid, je vais te vomir de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche.
fr.B: Mais tu es tiède, ni chaud ni froid ; c’est pourquoi je vais te vomir de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche.
fr.R: Mais tu es seulement tiède, ni chaud ni froid. Alors je vais te cracher hors de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche, comme de l’eau qui a mauvais goût.

decisions.choice: vomit out: utter rejection, said in the strongest picture
decisions.reason: ἐμέσαι means to vomit. Lukewarm water makes one want to spit it out, and Christ is about to reject the church in the same way. "I am about to" leaves room for the call to repent in 3:19.

decisions.choice: vomit (L); spew (B); spit (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the force of the Greek word. Balanced uses "spew", which keeps it strong; Readable uses a milder everyday word and adds the comparison with bad water.

decisions.choice: "vomir" (L, B); "cracher" (R)
decisions.reason: English Balanced has "spew", a strong word between "vomit" and "spit". French has no such middle word: "rejeter" and "recracher" lose the force of the picture (m1), so Balanced keeps "vomir" with Literal, and Readable uses the milder "cracher", as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὅτι λέγεις ὅτι Πλούσιός εἰμι καὶ πεπλούτηκα καὶ οὐδὲν χρείαν ἔχω, καὶ οὐκ οἶδας ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ταλαίπωρος καὶ ἐλεεινὸς καὶ πτωχὸς καὶ τυφλὸς καὶ γυμνός, συμβουλεύω σοι ἀγοράσαι παρ’ ἐμοῦ χρυσίον πεπυρωμένον ἐκ πυρὸς ἵνα πλουτήσῃς, καὶ ἱμάτια λευκὰ ἵνα περιβάλῃ καὶ μὴ φανερωθῇ ἡ αἰσχύνη τῆς γυμνότητός σου, καὶ κολλούριον ἐγχρῖσαι τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς σου ἵνα βλέπῃς.

records.literal_gloss: Because you say, Rich I am and I have grown rich and of nothing need I have, and not you know that you are the wretched and pitiable and poor and blind and naked, \v 18 I counsel you to buy from me gold having been refined by fire so that you may be rich, and garments white so that you may be clothed and not may be revealed the shame of the nakedness of you, and eye-salve to anoint the eyes of you so that you may see.

en.L: Because you say, 'I am rich, and I have become wealthy, and I have need of nothing,' and you do not know that you are the wretched one, and pitiable and poor and blind and naked, \v 18 I counsel you to buy from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gold refined by fire so that you may be rich, and white garments so that you may be clothed and the shame of your nakedness may not be revealed, and salve to anoint your eyes so that you may see.
en.B: You tell yourself, 'I am rich. I have built up my wealth, and I lack nothing.' You do not see that it is you who are wretched and to be pitied, poor and blind and naked. \v 18 So here is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} advice: buy from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gold that has been through the fire, and you will be rich; buy white garments and dress in them, and the shame of your nakedness will not be seen; and buy ointment for your eyes and put it on them, and you will see.
en.R: You say, 'I am rich. I have everything I want. I do not need anything.' But you do not know how bad things really are. You are miserable and pitiful. You are poor, blind, and naked. \v 18 So I advise you to buy gold from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, gold made pure in the fire. Then you will be truly rich. Buy white clothes from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to wear, so that you will not be ashamed of being naked. And buy medicine from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to put on your eyes, so that you can see.

fr.L: Parce que tu dis : “Je suis riche, je me suis enrichi et je n’ai besoin de rien”, et tu ne sais pas que c’est toi qui es le malheureux, et pitoyable, et pauvre, et aveugle, et nu, \v 18 je te conseille d’acheter auprès de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de l’or purifié par le feu afin que tu deviennes riche, et des vêtements blancs afin que tu sois vêtu et que la honte de ta nudité ne paraisse pas, et un collyre pour oindre tes yeux afin que tu voies.
fr.B: Tu te dis : “Je suis riche, j’ai amassé des biens, je ne manque de rien.” Tu ne vois pas que c’est toi qui es malheureux et digne de pitié, pauvre, aveugle et nu. \v 18 Voici donc {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} conseil : achète auprès de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} de l’or passé au feu, et tu seras riche ; achète des vêtements blancs et habille-toi, et la honte de ta nudité ne se verra pas ; achète un collyre et mets-le sur tes yeux, et tu verras.
fr.R: Tu dis : “Je suis riche. J’ai tout ce que je veux. Je n’ai besoin de rien.” Mais tu ne sais pas à quel point ta situation est grave. Tu es malheureux et pitoyable. Tu es pauvre, aveugle et nu. \v 18 Alors je te conseille d’acheter de l’or chez {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, de l’or purifié dans le feu. Ainsi tu seras vraiment riche. Achète chez {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} des vêtements blancs pour t’habiller, pour que tu n’aies pas la honte d’être nu. Et achète chez {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un remède à mettre sur tes yeux, pour que tu puisses voir.

decisions.choice: verses 17 and 18 are one sentence: "because you say ... I counsel you"
alternatives: verse 17 gives the reason for the threat in verse 16
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT runs 3:17-18 together, so "because you say" gives the reason for the advice in verse 18: since they think they are rich, Christ urges them to get true riches from him. ὅτι could also look back to verse 16 as the reason for the threat. The record follows the SBLGNT.

decisions.choice: wretched, pitiable, poor, blind and naked: their true state before God
decisions.reason: The church judges itself by its wealth. Christ names five things that show the opposite: it is to be pitied, poor in what counts, unable to see its state, and exposed to shame. The article before "wretched" makes it emphatic: you are the wretched one.

decisions.choice: buy from me: a call to get from Christ what the city could not supply
decisions.reason: To "buy" from one who has what they lack recalls Isaiah 55:1, where God invites those with no money to come and buy. Each thing to be bought answers a claim of the city (see the note on 3:14): gold refined by fire for true wealth (compare 1 Peter 1:7), white clothes for the shame of nakedness (3:4-5; 16:15), and salve for blind eyes.

decisions.choice: the sentence divided (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the long sentence (m1). Balanced and Readable divide it, as English needs, and begin verse 18 with "So" to show that the advice follows from verse 17.

source.text: ἐγὼ ὅσους ἐὰν φιλῶ ἐλέγχω καὶ παιδεύω· ζήλευε οὖν καὶ μετανόησον.

records.literal_gloss: I, as many as I love, I rebuke and discipline; be zealous therefore and repent.

en.L: I rebuke and discipline as many as I love. So be zealous and repent.
en.B: I correct and train all whom I love. Be eager, then, and repent.
en.R: I correct and train everyone I love. So be serious about it, and turn away from your sins.

fr.L: Moi, tous ceux que j’aime, je les reprends et je les corrige. Sois donc zélé et repens-toi.
fr.B: Je reprends et j’éduque tous ceux que j’aime. Sois donc plein d’ardeur, et repens-toi.
fr.R: Je corrige et j’éduque tous ceux que j’aime. Alors prends cela au sérieux, et détourne-toi de tes péchés.

decisions.choice: love that corrects: an echo of Proverbs 3:12
decisions.reason: Proverbs 3:12 says that the LORD disciplines those he loves, as a father the son he delights in (compare Hebrews 12:5-6). The hard words of the letter come from love. ἐλέγχω means to expose a fault and convict of it; παιδεύω is the training of a child.

decisions.choice: be zealous, and repent: an ongoing eagerness and a decisive turn
decisions.reason: ζήλευε is present: keep on being eager, the opposite of lukewarm. μετανόησον calls for a single decisive change, as in 2:5.

source.text: ἰδοὺ ἕστηκα ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν καὶ κρούω· ἐάν τις ἀκούσῃ τῆς φωνῆς μου καὶ ἀνοίξῃ τὴν θύραν, καὶ εἰσελεύσομαι πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ δειπνήσω μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς μετ’ ἐμοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Behold I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears the voice of me and opens the door, I will come in to him and I will dine with him and he with me.

en.L: Look, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and opens the door, I will come in to {{gender:that person|him}} and eat with {{gender:that person|him}}, and {{gender:that person|he}} with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Look: I am standing at the door, knocking. If anyone hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and opens the door, I will come in and share a meal with {{gender:them|him}}, and {{gender:they|he}} with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Listen! I am standing at the door and knocking. If anyone hears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice and opens the door, I will come in. We will eat together as friends.

fr.L: Voici, je suis debout à la porte et je frappe. Si quelqu’un entend {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix et ouvre la porte, j’entrerai chez lui et je dînerai avec lui, et lui avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Voici : je me tiens devant la porte, et je frappe. Si quelqu’un entend {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix et ouvre la porte, j’entrerai, je prendrai le repas avec lui, et lui avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Écoute ! Je suis là, devant la porte, et je frappe. Si quelqu’un entend {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} voix et ouvre la porte, j’entrerai. Nous mangerons ensemble, comme des amis.

decisions.choice: standing at the door: Christ seeks entry to a church that has shut him out
alternatives: standing at the door at his final coming (compare James 5:9)
decisions.reason: The letter is to a church, and Christ stands outside its door asking to come in. The offer is made to "anyone", each person in the church. Some read it of his final coming, when he is "at the door" (Mark 13:29; James 5:9); the call to hear and open fits a present invitation better.

decisions.choice: eating together: the closest fellowship
decisions.reason: δειπνήσω is the main meal of the day, eaten in the evening. To share it meant friendship and welcome. Jesus also spoke of eating with his followers in his kingdom (Luke 22:29-30), and Revelation 19:9 speaks of the wedding supper of the Lamb.

decisions.choice: as friends (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what sharing a meal meant (m2) in place of the repeated "and he with me".

source.text: ὁ νικῶν δώσω αὐτῷ καθίσαι μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ μου, ὡς κἀγὼ ἐνίκησα καὶ ἐκάθισα μετὰ τοῦ πατρός μου ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] overcoming, I will give to him to sit with me on the throne of me, as I also overcame and sat with the Father of me on the throne of him.

en.L: The one who overcomes, I will give {{gender:that person|him}} [the right] to sit with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, as I also overcame and sat down with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.
en.B: To everyone who overcomes I will give a place beside {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne, just as I overcame and took {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} seat beside {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.
en.R: I will let everyone who wins the victory sit with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} throne. In the same way, I won the victory and sat down with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.

fr.L: Celui qui est vainqueur, je lui donnerai [le droit] de s’asseoir avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} trône, comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi j’ai été vainqueur et je me suis assis avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône.
fr.B: À tout vainqueur je donnerai une place à côté de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} trône, de même que j’ai été vainqueur et que j’ai pris place à côté de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône.
fr.R: Je permettrai à tous ceux qui remportent la victoire de s’asseoir avec {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} sur {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} trône. De la même manière, j’ai remporté la victoire et je me suis assis avec {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône.

decisions.choice: Christ's victory and his throne: the pattern for those who follow him
decisions.reason: Christ overcame by his death and resurrection (5:5-6) and sat down with his Father on his throne (compare Psalm 110:1; Hebrews 12:2). Those who overcome as he did will share his rule (2:26-27; 20:4; 22:5). Revelation speaks of one throne of God and of the Lamb (22:1, 3). This last promise sums up the promises of all seven letters.

decisions.choice: a place beside me (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "a place beside me" to give the sense of sharing the throne, not merely sitting near it.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

en.L: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
en.B: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."
en.R: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches."

fr.L: Que celui qui a une oreille entende ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.B: Que celui qui a des oreilles écoute ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »
fr.R: Que tous ceux qui peuvent entendre écoutent bien ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises. »

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.
